cell_type.evidence: inferred: Alcohol consumption induces hepatocyte damage through complex processes involving oxidative stress and disrupted metabolism.

disease_state.evidence: A chronic murine model of ALD was employed to quantify hepatic cysteine redox and lysine acetylation, revealing that alcohol metabolism significantly reduced the cysteine proteome and increased protein acetylation.

Furthermore, these unique Cys-Lys redox signatures are translationally relevant as revealed by orthologous comparison with severe alcohol-associated hepatitis (SAH) explants, revealing numerous pathogenic thiol redox signals in these patients.

material_type.evidence: Whole liver samples (n=5) were homogenized by bead milling using a Qiagen TissueLyser LT set to 50 Hz for 6 minutes.

sample_source.evidence: The pair-fed control and alcohol-fed murine hepatic peptides were combined 1:1 and were used to generate an accurate mass and retention time (AMRT) library(9).
